Tuned vs TiviMate

November 19, 2026

TiviMate, from Armobsoft, is the player many people try first on an Android TV box, and for good reason: it has a polished grid guide, recording and catch-up. Tuned covers the same ground on a TV and adds phones, tablets, offline downloads and film details. Here is how they compare, using what each developer says.

At a glance

TiviMateTuned
Where it runsAndroid TV; the developer says it isn't made for phones or tabletsAndroid phones, tablets, Chromebooks, Android TV and Google TV
Playlist typesM3U, Xtream Codes, Stalker portal; several playlistsXtream Codes, M3U link or file, MAC portal, Plex, Jellyfin and Emby
TV guideGrid guideXMLTV guide as a list or a full grid, with reminders
Catch-upYesYes, on Xtream servers that keep recordings
RecordingYesYes, live and from the guide (Premium)
Pause and rewind live TVNot stated by the developerYes, up to an hour kept on the device (Premium)
Several channels at onceYes, several channels on one screenNo, on purpose: one stream connection at a time
Casting to a TVNot stated by the developerChromecast and DLNA, phone as remote
Picture-in-pictureNot stated by the developerYes
Offline downloadsNot stated by the developerFilms and episodes, whole seasons too (more than 3 at a time is Premium)
Profiles and parental controlsParental controlsUp to 6 profiles, kids profiles and PINs (Premium); adult categories locked behind a PIN
TraktNot stated by the developerTrakt and Simkl; Trakt can import watched history (Premium)
Film and show detailsNot stated by the developerTMDB ratings, trailers, cast and actor pages, saved on the device
SubtitlesNot stated by the developerFull caption styling, timing fix, and subtitle search for films and episodes
AdsNot stated by the developerNone, ever
PriceFree to try; Premium about US$9.99 a year or US$33.99 once, up to 5 devices (third-party guides)Free; Premium US$9.99 a year with a 7-day trial, or US$24.99 once

"Not stated by the developer" means we couldn't find it on the developer's own pages or store listing. It may still be there, so check before you rule it out.

Price

TiviMate is free to install, and Premium unlocks most of what people use it for. The developer's pages we read don't list a price. Guides that track it put Premium at about US$9.99 a year, with a short trial, or about US$33.99 once, covering up to five devices, bought through the TiviMate Companion app on a phone. Tuned is free, with Premium at US$9.99 a year with a 7-day trial or US$24.99 once.

Tuned's prices are what Google Play charges in the United States; Play shows them in your own currency. Premium covers up to three devices, and a Tuned account can add more.

Where TiviMate is ahead

  • Multi-view. TiviMate can show several channels on one screen. Tuned never will, because each extra channel is another connection to your provider.
  • Stalker portals for everything. Tuned's MAC portal sign-in covers live TV and its guide only, for now.
  • A long track record on Android TV and a guide grid that many people already know.

Where Tuned is ahead

  • Phones and tablets. TiviMate's own listing says it isn't built for touch screens. Tuned is the same app on a phone, a tablet and a TV, with layouts for each.
  • Offline downloads of films, episodes and whole seasons, played from the device.
  • Film and show pages with TMDB ratings, trailers and cast, plus Trakt and Simkl.
  • Subtitle search and timing for films and episodes.

What Tuned does that most players don't

  • Opens straight to your channels. The playlist and guide live on the device, so the app shows channels the moment it opens and keeps them fresh in the background. Lists page straight from the database, so a playlist with tens of thousands of streams scrolls smoothly.
  • One stream connection, ever. The player, downloads, recordings, channel scans and backup copies take turns on a single connection, and anything in the background waits while you watch. Providers limit connections per account, and Tuned never uses a second one.
  • Live events from your guide. Today's games and fights are pulled out of the guide into one page. Tune finds a working English stream for an event, one channel at a time, and you can follow a team, league or fighter to get an alert before they play.
  • Backup copies and dead channels. When a channel has several copies, Tuned tries the next one if the first won't play, and a channel scan hides channels that never work, without blaming them for a slow internet connection or a busy server.
  • Real names over numbers. Episodes show their real titles from TMDB rather than "S1 E1", and tapping an actor opens everything they've been in, with what's in your playlist marked.
  • Sign in on a TV with your phone. Scan a QR code on the TV and type the login on your phone instead of with the remote.

Which one to pick

If you only watch on an Android TV box and want several channels on one screen, TiviMate does that and Tuned doesn't. If you watch on a phone or tablet as well, want downloads and film details, or want an app that never opens a second connection to your provider, try Tuned.

Checked on 19 November 2026. Features and prices change, so check the developer's page before you buy.
